description: The client-server frame protocol every id shell (terminal, web, native) speaks to a world host. Version 1 is the protocol behind the /id-world/1 ALPN. A shell sends only frames and fields named here; it ignores server frame types and fields it does not know. Additive changes bump `revision`; removing or changing a frame or field needs version 2 and a new ALPN. Event-producing frames must name their stable world-event contract here.

websocket.envelope: text-message; binary-message for negotiated binary view patches (revision 12)

ssh-exec.session: one SSH session channel running the exec command

phases.opening: The session's first frame. It may carry the `world` routing field; absent means the host's default world.
phases.query: After an opening query frame: further query frames, or a join.
phases.install: After install_begin was answered with upload_ready: chunks, then install_end.
phases.joined: From the frame after a join. A shell may send joined-phase frames (such as its first resize) before the snapshot arrives; the host reads them once the join is answered. Every frame keeps the session joined.

classes.event: Becomes one committed world event: journaled, replayed, and delivered to sessions through the client projection.
classes.ephemeral: Connection-local presentation context. Never journaled and never seen by other sessions.
classes.query: Read-only. Never journaled and never changes the world.
classes.control: Session lifecycle. The frame itself is never journaled.
classes.admin: Authority-bearing configuration. Needs the admin secret or a signed moderator request, and may write a journal entry.
classes.delegation: Mints a narrower capability from the session's own. It may write a journal entry; it never widens authority.

projection.description: Every server frame is built from the one client projection (F11.11). A program seed never reaches a session: any `seed` key in a server frame must be 0.

features.screen_msgpack: Revision 12 (negotiated binary screen patches, F12.11 phase 3, issue #12242; design doc/2026-11-01_design_id805.md sections 3, 5, 6): the join frame's `screen_msgpack` field is the capability flag — a shell that sets it, together with `screen_patches`, on a byte-capable transport receives screen patch frames as binary frames instead of JSON `view` frames. A binary patch frame is one versioned MessagePack value (id-core `screen_codec`, codec version 1) carrying exactly the fields of the `view` frame it replaces — `sequence`, `view_revision`, `base_view_revision`, `resume_token`, and the `patch` — with the same world-event cursor and view-revision semantics; full views, resume-token issuance, and every other frame stay on the text path. On the length-prefixed transports (iroh, ssh-exec) a binary frame body is marked with a single leading NUL byte, which no JSON text frame can start with; on WebSocket it is a binary message. Negotiation is offer-and-observe: a host or transport without the revision simply keeps sending JSON patch frames, and a shell must accept both for a session that offered the flag. Client frames remain text JSON in both directions of the negotiation; a binary frame from a client is malformed input and fails the session safely, like a non-UTF-8 frame. A host never sends a binary frame to a session that did not offer the flag, and never guesses an encoding: an unsupported codec version or a malformed binary payload is a decode failure for the shell, which falls back to a full view by rejoining or presenting its retained full-view path.
features.agent_profile: Revision 11 (agent profile for #6300, design doc/2026-11-09_design_id6300_agents_in_worlds_v1.md sections 4.2, 4.3, 8, 9.1): the capability flag is the join frame's `agent_profile` field — a shell that sets it advertises it can consume semantic diffs. A joined agent-profile shell may send `screen_subscribe` naming a screen region (an object with u16 `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` in screen cells) and/or semantic event classes (`chat_posted`, `input_applied`, `object_changed`, `system_event`, `program_changed`; an empty list means all classes, an absent field means no event diffs). The host answers with a `screen_subscription` frame echoing the active subscription and the current screen revision, then sends `semantic_diff` frames scoped to the subscription: event diffs for subscribed classes as world events commit, and region diffs (changes of kind `region_changed`, one per changed row inside the region, carrying that row's new text) as views change. Each semantic_diff names the world `sequence` it follows, the `view_revision` it was computed at, and its `base_view_revision` when it diffs against a known earlier screen. Agent input frames (`input`, `chat`, `paste`, `form_result`, `pointer`) may carry `screen_revision`, the stale-decision token: the screen revision the input was decided against. The host applies such an input only while that revision is still the session's current screen revision; otherwise it rejects the input with an `error` frame whose code is `stale_decision`, commits nothing, and returns the current view. A host without this revision does not know the flag and serves the agent full view frames at reduced fidelity with identical authority; a shell that never sets the flag is unaffected.
features.surface: A view frame may carry a typed `surface` (the portable screen document). A shell that does not understand it renders `data`.
features.input_events: Pointer input per the input event model design (doc/2026-11-08T05-48-47Z_design_input_event_model, issue #1831 slice S2; landed in revision 10). Coordinates are cells in the target surface's grid: producers map device pixels to cells at the edge, so frames never carry pixels. `pointer` frames are class event — journaled and replayed like `input`; a drag is a press, a sequence of drag_move frames, and a release, and each drag_move is its own frame, so the frame limit bounds one move, never the whole path. `hover` frames are class ephemeral: connection-local presentation context, never journaled and never seen by other sessions. A pointer_id is unique only within its producing connection; the host namespaces it with the connection's identity when journaling, and press/release pairing is scoped to that (connection, pointer_id) pair. An event an environment cannot produce, or that the target app did not declare in its manifest `interfaces.input`, is refused explicitly: the host answers `input_refused` naming the event and a reason from that frame's enum — an input event is never silently dropped.

reserved.presentation_tiers: In-band terminal tier detection and negotiation (F13.4). Needs a new frame kind, so it waits for F11.12.
reserved.focus: A focus frame for typed input (F13.4/F13.5). Not in version 1.
reserved.client_providers: Client-side capability requests and replies (F13.7). The offer/request/reply frames landed in revision 9 (F13.7 step 2); the broker that sends requests is F13.7 step 3.
